class: A test double (a stand-in model, a fake server, a socket fake) is written from the builder's assumption of the real thing - an older protocol, a different base class - so tests pass against the double while the real thing fails, or tests fail against the double while the real thing works; the double is not checked against the real implementation it imitates.
mechanism: (1) Row 23a: the Execute seq-echo test used a plain BaseModel stand-in for ExecuteOut; the real class is an ApiModel whose model_copy raises, so every Execute with seq crashed while the test passed. (2) Row 24: the page began dropping live pushes without the version it sent; the Vitest socket fakes were updated, but two Playwright specs that play the server themselves (execute-screen.spec.ts, feed-reconnect.spec.ts) kept sending pushes without seq, so CI failed while the real server was right.

first_seen.where: row 23a round-2 check (stand-in base class) and CI App tests run 40083846807 on 7f86296a (row 24 e2e fakes)
first_seen.evidence: 23a: probe with an ApiModel stand-in -> TypeError model_copy(update=...) skips validation. Row 24: execute-screen.spec.ts:18 'no Execute action: phase=waiting-live'; feed-reconnect.spec.ts:23 data-live 'connecting' instead of 'live'.

fix: Instances fixed (23a: the test drives a real ExecuteOut; row 24: one e2e helper echoes seq like live_push.py). Class mechanism (second occurrence - Learn-or-block): a repo test that fails when a Playwright spec answers `**/api/strategies/live` itself without the shared echo helper, and a brief standing item: every double named in a test is built from, or checked against, the real class or server behaviour.

detection.note: Guarded for the Playwright half only: tests/test_e2e_live_socket_fakes.py refuses any send on the strategy live socket (in a file whose routeWebSocket pattern can match /api/strategies/live, or a support file it imports) that is not stamped by the shared echoSeq helper, a pure forward or a client socket. Out of reach: a send through a computed property built at run time, a socket whose URL cannot match the live one, a non-relative or re-exported import. The stand-in-class half (row 23a: a double built from an assumed base class) is covered by the builder-brief standing item, a brief line and not a test, so it is not machine-checked. Two occurrences on 2026-10-24; CI e2e caught the second one; the first was caught by an independent check only.

occurrences.evidence: two Playwright strategy-socket fakes without seq
